review: Game is a real mixed bag. On the one hand it does much of the core gameplay loop very well; the process of developing and maintaining software is pretty engaging and does mirror real life fairly closely. Making offices is cool too but I can't be bothered to put much time into it personally. My main gripe is software features - you can't actually release a fully functioning software (as far as modern standards go) without kneecapping your profitability/how long the dev cycle is. It totally takes me out of the game to have a DAW with synthesizers and mixing but no drum sequencer for example. No company would ever release software with such a limited feature set and call it a DAW. This applies to every software category. The worst part is, there used to be a much better system which the dev for some reason scrapped and has furthermore made said system untouchable by mods. This game might be good for one or two playthroughs, but I really wouldn't recommend it currently given this core design flaw.

Software Inc. — отзыв

Общая оценка: 6/10

Графика: 4/5
Геймплей: 3/5
Звук: 3/5

Когда-то давно я проходил мимо этой игры и думал: «О, симулятор IT-компании, круто, построю свой офис, найму крутых разрабов, выпущу софт-бестселлер и уйду на пенсию в 40 лет». На практике оказалось, что это не симулятор IT-бизнеса, а симулятор ждуна.

Бóльшая часть игры — это совершенно бездарное ожидание. Ждёшь, пока твои сотрудники допишут строчки кода. Ждёшь, пока закончится найм. Ждёшь, пока офис построится. Ждёшь, пока рынок подрастёт. Ждёшь, пока обновятся лиды. И так по кругу.

Сам процесс найма и развития персонала — интересный, менеджмент проектов тоже может зацепить, если вы любитель покопаться в механиках. Но темп игры убийственный. Даже на максимальной скорости всё ползёт как сонная муха. А если у тебя больше одного проекта в работе — готовься ставить чайник, пока ждёшь, когда твои криворукие джуны наконец отладят баги в версии 1.03.

Начинается всё бодро, а где-то к середине наступает момент осознания: я сижу и смотрю, как ползут полоски прогресса. Это не игра — это тайм-менеджмент с элементами сидения у аквариума.

Из плюсов: приятная пиксельная графика, хорошая кастомизация и глубокая экономическая система. Если у вас вагон свободного времени и вы готовы медитировать на полоски загрузки — заходите. Если хотите динамики — проходите мимо.

6/10 — идея отличная, реализация могла бы быть быстрее и динамичнее.

I've sunk over 85 hours into Software Inc and I'm still finding new layers to it. This is hands-down the best business sim I've played since the original Game Dev Tycoon, and honestly it leaves most of the genre in the dust.
What sets it apart is the depth without the bloat. You start in a garage with a couple of underpaid coders cranking out shareware, and before you know it you're running a multi-floor office complex, juggling OS development, console hardware, marketing campaigns, employee training programs, and a stock-market IPO. Every system actually matters. Office layout affects employee mood. Mood affects work speed and bug rates. Bug rates affect reviews. Reviews affect sales. It all interlocks beautifully without ever feeling like spreadsheet hell.
The art style is clean and readable, the building tools are genuinely fun (I've spent entire evenings just designing campuses), and the AI competitors keep you on your toes — releasing rival operating systems, poaching your best designers, pricing you out of markets. The era progression from the late 70s into the modern day gives the whole thing a satisfying arc.
Special shoutout to the developer, Coredumping, who has supported this game with consistent updates for years. The modding community is also fantastic if you want to extend the experience further.
If you've ever fantasized about being the next Bill Gates, or you just love games where you can lose six hours optimizing an HVAC system for a server room, buy it. You won't regret it.
Verdict: Absolute gem. Buy it on sale, buy it at full price — just buy it.

This review hurts to write.

Software Inc is one of the most in-depth and replayable software development simulators available. It has systems that allow for far more emergent behavior than most other games in the genre. That is exactly why this is so frustrating.

Over time, the game has added more and more mechanics that pull attention away from actually developing software. What used to feel somewhat focused has been cluttered by unnecessary mechanics. Instead of spending most of my time producing software, I am managing a growing list of systems that feel only loosely related to the core loop.

I do not have an issue with depth. The issue is how much of it is forced on the player at once. The experience now feels bloated and, at times, exhausting to play. It is no longer just a software simulator. It feels like I am constantly balancing an office simulation just to get to the part I actually enjoy.

Earlier versions of the game felt far more centered around software development, which makes this shift very noticeable.

The biggest problem is that there is no way to opt out of these mechanics. If players were given the ability to disable or scale back certain systems, this would be far less of an issue. As it stands, they are mandatory, and they drag down the overall experience.

Despite its depth and replayability, I do not find the game enjoyable to play in its current state.

A proposta de Software Inc. é, no papel, extremamente atraente. A ideia de criar e gerenciar sua própria empresa de software chama atenção até de quem não é da área — e, para quem é, parece quase irresistível.

Mesmo assim, minha experiência acabou sendo mais frustrante do que envolvente.

Insisti no jogo por um bom tempo, cerca de 20 horas de gameplay e nada. Curiosamente, a parte que mais funcionou pra mim foi a mais simples: ganhar dinheiro com contratos, sem funcionários. É onde o jogo parece mais direto e menos punitivo.

Já o core da experiência, criar um software do zero, é pesado. Muito pesado. A sensação é quase a de “parir uma bigorna”: exige estudo, planejamento e entendimento de mecânicas que não são nada triviais. Não é algo que você pega e joga de forma leve.

O problema é que isso vem acompanhado de um nível alto de microgerenciamento operacional. Você passa mais tempo lidando com processos, prazos e detalhes do que tomando decisões estratégicas interessantes.

E ainda tem o fator tempo: o jogo praticamente te obriga a jogar em fast forward, mas isso vira uma armadilha. Se você piscar, perde prazos de desenvolvimento, datas de release ou entregas importantes, o que gera mais frustração do que desafio.

No fim, fica aquela sensação de que o jogo é profundo, mas pouco acessível. Ele exige dedicação quase como uma ferramenta de trabalho, e não como entretenimento.

Conclusão:
Uma ideia excelente, com potencial enorme, mas que acaba se perdendo na complexidade e no excesso de operacional. Não é um jogo leve e, pelo menos pra mim, não conseguiu justificar o investimento de tempo. Não sei se voltarei a jogar.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game to anyone in its current state.

This game has been in development for a very long time, and while I appreciate the addition of features and dedication to making this game better, this strategy can also HARM a game, which is exactly what happened here.

At some point, the features become overhwleming and bloat the game needlessly, especially if there isn't a carefully implemented balance to keep them at bay. This game has no balance. It doesn't feel like anything other than what it was ten years ago. Sure, there are many new features, but they feel hollow and superficial.

As a great example, take a look at marketing. This is quite possible the worst mechanic in the game, with no rhyme or reason to it. It often feels like something hastily slapped on rather than a deep and well made mechanic added over the years.

There is a large focus on building and mild simulation in terms of taking care of the people running around, but I can't help and compare it to the Sims. Side by side, even though this game is about business and not life simulation, this pales in comparison to the Sims 2 or 3 or 4. The building mehcanics feel clunky, the simulation mechanics feel useless, and when you finally jump into the business management, it becomes a game played through ugly UI's and wittles down to clickers and sliders.

The UI's and their ugliness cannot be overstated. They are also poorly designed and organized, making you root around endlessly to find things that should have been easier to access. 

If you absolutely love micromangement this game might scratch that itch for you, but it falls woefully short of being an in depth business simulation like some people make it out to be. I've played games both much more simplistic and more complicated than this game, and had fun with them more than I did here. So the issue isn't complexity, it's design.

Game Dev Tycoon is a much more bare bones game, for example, and yet it was designed well and looks more appealing than SoftWare Inc., and I enjoyed it a lot more.

Capitalism Lab is a much more complex game, but has some outdated visuals, and yet its depth allows for better roleplaying than with Software Inc.

I don't know if the dev hasn't taken this game out of EA because he doesn't feel it has hit that sweet spot, but I suspect that is a reason. You can feel that the balance is off and there is no dopamine rush once you hit any of your accomplishments here. It doesn't feel earned. In fact, the game is extremely exploitable through its stock market and contract based system. You do not need to do anything else to become rich within the first few months of play. It's a fundemanetally broken system that the dev refuses to fix.

The achievements are extremely lacking. This has been in development for a decade, and there are less achievements for this game than games with a dev time of one or two years. It is probably trivial to add more achievements, and yet the dev won't do it. This speaks volumes about the level of care the dev is putting into this game. People often point to the long dev time and early access period as evidence of caring, but it can just as easily be the opposite. Countless poorly made features are a sign of neglect, not dedication. I'd rather have a much more bare bones game done well with tons of achievments, than a bloated game with useless mechanics.

Finally, the tutorials in this game are abysmal. This cannot be understated. This game has become so complex that new users frequently have to watch hours of youtube footage just to learn the basic mechanics. While this is fine for deep and complex games with good design, it doesn't quite work here and only makes this game more frustrating to get into. The tutorials provided in the game through the ugly and clunky UI system are bare bones and only give you the bare minimum. They don't properly show you how to play, rather they tell you where to click to get the tutorial over with. There are many mechanics that are not properly or adequately explained in the game, or are glossed over entirely.

For these reasons, this is not a game I enjoyed or will come back to.
